intended_object: Take a Huber ring A with a pair of definition (A₀, I), and the rational localisation A_s with numerators T. The object is the ideal J = I·D of the candidate ring of definition D = A₀[T/s] ⊆ A_s, meaning the ideal of D generated by the image of I. This comes from the docstring and the module's construction of the topology on the rational localisation (Wedhorn §8, Huber).
explanation: `locSubring P T s S` is defined as `Algebra.adjoin A₀ {t/s : t ∈ T}`, viewed as a subring of S. That is exactly D = A₀[T/s]. `toLocSubring` is the map A₀ → A → S, with its codomain cut down to D; this works because D contains the image of A₀. `locIdeal` is then `Ideal.map toLocSubring I`, the ideal of D generated by the image of I. In the textbook notation this is I·D. It is the standard ideal of definition of D in the construction of the topology on A⟨T/s⟩ (Huber; Wedhorn Prop. 8.2). The surrounding lemmas match this reading: `fg_locIdeal` and `locIdeal_pow` are proved, and `isAdic_locIdeal` is announced, all as in the literature. The setting is already as general as the notion: a commutative topological ring with a pair of definition, and any model S of the localisation away from s. Mathlib has no Huber-ring localisation, and the general step is just `Ideal.map`, which the definition reuses rather than rewriting.
